REPORT
Date February 21, 1933

Subject (in full) Illegal functioning in the Settlement by members
of Public Safety Bureau.

Made by Supt. Tan Shao Liang Forwarded by *Jno Robertson, Supt*

In compliance with instructions I called on
Gen. Wen Ung En at his office (Public Safety Bureau
headquarters) at 4 p.m. February 20 and after briefly
relating unfortunate incidents mentioned in the
attached reports, requested him to take measures to
avoid a repetition. Gen. Wen in the presence of his
secretary Col. Paul Lee replied he would give the
necessary instructions. With your approval I gave
Col. Lee a copy of the attached ~~report~~ memorandum.

*Tan Shaoliang*
Superintendent.

Officer i/c special Branch.

*Commissioner of Police,*
Sir,
Information.

*J.M. Owens*
O. i/c Sp. Br.
FEB 21 1933

page_data.en:
Memorandum on Recent Cases of Illegal Functioning in
the Settlement by members of the Chinese Authorities.

D. 4454
(1) Shortly after 3.30 p.m. February 1, 1933, a party
of Police from Bubbling Well Station in answer to a call
proceeded to House No. 5, Lane 56, Medhurst Road, where
it was ascertained that Inspector Lieu Kuh Jing ( 婁克敬 )
attached to the Political Branch of the Shanghai Public
Safety Bureau, in company with certain Chinese males,
had entered the premises and effected the arrest of two
male and one female Chinese communists and in doing so,
had seriously injured the two former persons. Neither
Inspector Lieu or any of his collegues informed any
member of the Municipal Police that they were watching
or had suspicions against people living in this neighbour-
hood, and they failed to tell the police station concerned
or even police on street duty in the vicinity that they
intended to enter the house.

At the entrance of this particular alleyway a
Chinese Police Watchman was stationed, and Lieu could
have requested this individual to either help him or obtain
assistance from a Police Station.

D 4519
(2) The Municipal Police while searching the passengers
on a tram car on Ichang Road at 6.25 p.m. February 14, 1933
found one Tai Yung Tsing ( 戴永清 ) accompanied by Dzung
Yi Tsi ( 鍾義慈 ), in possession of a loaded .25 Automatic
Pistol--Make BREVET, No.4403-- for which he possessed
no license or permit from the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Tai and Dzung, who turned out to be detectives attached
to the Political Branch of the Shanghai Public Safety
Bureau Headquarters, were subsequently handed over to
the 6th Division of the Public Safety Bureau.
page_data.zh:
关于中国当局成员近期在租界内非法活动的备忘录。

D. 4454
(1) 1933年2月1日下午3点30分过后不久，静安寺捕房的一队警察接到报警后前往麦特赫斯特路56弄5号，经查实，隶属于上海公共安全局政治科的娄克敬督察与若干中国男子进入该处，逮捕了两名男性和一名女性中国共产党人，在此过程中严重伤害了前两名男性。娄督察及其同事均未通知任何工部局警务人员他们正在监视或怀疑居住在该地区的人员，也未告知相关捕房甚至附近执勤的巡警他们打算进入该房屋。

在该弄堂入口处有一名中国巡更值守，娄本可以请求此人协助或从捕房获得援助。

D 4519
(2) 1933年2月14日下午6点25分，工部局警务人员在宜昌路一辆电车上搜查乘客时，发现戴永清由鍾義慈陪同，持有一支装弹的.25口径自动手枪——品牌为BREVET，编号4403——他并未持有上海公共租界工部局颁发的执照或许可证。戴和鍾后来被证实是隶属于上海公共安全局总部政治科的侦探，随后被移交给公共安全局第六科。

page_data.en:
(2)
D 4527. (3) At 5.10 p.m. February 17, 1933, Detective Sub-
Inspector Tsang Yue Loong (曾雨龍) and Detective Sergeant
Woo Zau Shang (何少章), attached to the 4th Station,
5th Division, Public Safety Bureau, Yingshiangkong,
arrested one Iung Ching Shang (柳正昌), overseer
employed at the Dong Shing (同興) Cotton Mill
(Japanese), No. 2086 Yangtszepoo Road, outside the
mill premises, on the authority of confidential order,
character Mi (密) No. 4, issued by the Chief of the
Shanghai Public Safety Bureau on a charge of having
acted as a spy for the Headquarters of the 3rd
Company of the Japanese Marines during the Sino-
Japanese incident. After effecting the arrest, they
brought the prisoner to the station with the assistance
of C.P.C.s 2798 and 2314. It was there discovered
that both Sub-Inspector Tsang and Sergeant Woo were
armed. Although these officers obviously came to
Yangtszepoo District for the specific purpose of
effecting this arrest, they failed to convey any
information whatever of their plans or intentions to
the Municipal Police or to report that they were coming
into the Settlement bearing arms.
page_data.zh:
(2)
D 4527. (3) 1933年2月17日下午5点10分，隶属于引翔港第五分区第四捕房的侦探副督察曾雨龍和侦探警长何少章，依据上海公共安全局局长签发的代字“密”第4号秘密命令，以在中日事变期间担任日本海军陆战队第三大队总部间谍的罪名，在杨树浦路2086号同興棉纱厂（日资）厂门外逮捕了该厂监工柳正昌。实施逮捕后，他们在华捕2798号和2314号的协助下将囚犯带至捕房。此时发现曾副督察和何警长均携带武器。虽然这些官员显然是为了实施此次逮捕而特意来到杨树浦区的，但他们未向工部局警务处通报其计划或意图的任何信息，也未报告他们携带武器进入租界。

page_data.en:
Copy of Yangtszepoo Daily Report of February 18, 1933.

ILLEGAL FUNCTIONING
AND ILLEGAL ARREST
BY CHINESE OFFICIALS.

At 5.10 p.m. on February 17 while C.P.Cs.
2798 and 2314 were on duty on Yangtszepoo Road
near Kwangshin Road, they were called on by one
Woo Zau Hyang, a Chinese Sergeant No.387 of the
4th Division, 5th District, Ying Ziang Kong, to
take into custody a Chinese foreman of the Dong
Shing Cotton Mill, 2086 Yangtszepoo Road, whom he
had arrested on the footpath outside the Mill with
the assistance of his two colleagues. All the
Chinese Police were in plain clothes.

All concerned were brought to the Police
Station, and from enquiries made it was ascertained
that a confidential memo. issued by the Commission-
er of the Public Safety Bureau on February 9 and
forwarded to the Inspector i/c of the 4th Station,
5th Division, gave orders to make strict and con-
fidential investigations re this man and four
others, whose names are mentioned in the document
for having been traitors during the Sino-Japanese
hostilities. Acting on this authority only the
arrest was effected. Following the arrest some
resistance was offered by the foreman and he was
handcuffed. This drew a crowd of mill hands,
also some Japanese employees of the Mill. It
was then that the two C.P.Cs. were called to the
scene, when the crowd quietly dispersed. One of
the Japanese employees referred to alleged that
the Chinese sergeant Woo Zau Hyang, brandished his
pistol towards the crowd which gathered about, but
there is no corroboration in this respect, though
Woo admitted taking his pistol from his pocket and
holding it in his hand, as he was frightened the
crowd would rescue the man in custody.

As the man was arrested illegally he was
released.
page_data.zh:
1933年2月18日杨树浦日报表副本。

中国官员的
非法活动及
非法逮捕。

2月17日下午5点10分，当华捕2798号和2314号在杨树浦路靠近广信路处执勤时，一名来自引翔港第五区第四分队的中国警长吴少香（编号387）叫住他们，要求拘留同兴棉纱厂（杨树浦路2086号）的一名中国监工，该监工是在其两名同事的协助下在厂外人行道上被捕的。所有中国警察均着便衣。

所有相关人员都被带到捕房，经查询获悉，公共安全局局长于2月9日签发并发送给第五分区第四捕房主管督察的一份秘密备忘录，命令对此人及文件中提及的另外四人进行严格且秘密的调查，指控他们在中日敌对行动期间充当叛徒。仅依据此授权实施了逮捕。逮捕后，该监工进行了反抗，因此被戴上手铐。这引来了一群工厂工人，以及一些日籍职员。此时两名华捕被叫到现场，人群随即安静地散去。上述一名日籍职员称，中国警长吴少香向聚集的人群挥舞手枪，但在这方面没有佐证，尽管吴承认因担心人群会劫走被拘留者而感到害怕，所以从口袋里掏出手枪拿在手中。

由于该男子是被非法逮捕的，故予以释放。

page_data.en:
Character Mi (密) No.4
Time 3:30 p.m.
Confidential Order Date 9/2/33 (22nd Republic Years).
- Acting on 1st Confidential Intelligence Report dated Feb.
9th, this confidential order is issued for the arrest of:-
Traitor Zung Tien Oong (张天鸿), alias Woo Shaun (吴尚),
native of Ningpo, age 30 odd, residing in 3rd mill quarters,
of the Shi Ho Cotton Mill, Western District, Shanghai.
During the Sino-Japanese Hostilities, January 28th, 1932, he,
under the pretext of enlisting and employing of Chinese workers,
secretly recruited men to organize snipers' squads. He sold
indecent pictures to Japanese soldiers — an action detrimental
to the Country's Reputation. He disclosed to Japanese army the
military secrets of Chinese army. He together with a Japanese
named Heshizima to the Japanese Military Headquarters where he
acted as a Chinese Interpreter to question those Chinese arrest-
ed by the Japanese. He also accompanied Japanese to visit
Kingkong, Poh Sing Ching, Kwenshan, Liu Ho, important military
strategic points under the pretext of shooting birds with a view
to taking the Japanese there to draw maps.
Traitor Wong Yung Zien (王荣钱), age 30 odd, native of
Ningpo, residing No.1 Mill quarters, Kung Dah Cotton Mill, Y'Poo.
He was formerly inspector of the said mill. He was spy to the
Japanese army during Jan. 28th, 1932. Afterwards he took
Japanese airplane to direct army to bomb Kiangwan. He also led
bad characters to rob money and things in the war area. He also
employed 300 and/or 400 Chinese workmen on behalf of the
Japanese army to raise and flat waste ground on the back of the
Kang Dah Cotton Mill and make it an aerodrome.
The 3 following traitors were acting as spies for the Head-
Quarters of the 3rd Company of the Japanese Marines:-
(1) Zee Chi Cheng (谢志成), age 35/9, residing No.29 Tung Hai
Lee, Tungchow Road.
(2) Ying Ching Shiang (应清祥), age 37, native of Anhwei,
residing No.66, Tung Shing Cotton Mill quarters, Y'Poo Road.
page_data.zh:
代字“密”第4号
时间 下午3:30
秘密命令日期 1933年2月9日（民国二十二年）。
- 根据2月9日的第一份秘密情报报告，发布此秘密命令以逮捕以下人员：
叛徒张天鸿，别名吴尚，宁波人，三十多岁，居住在上海西区世和棉纱厂第三宿舍。在1932年1月28日的中日敌对行动期间，他以招募和雇佣中国工人为借口，秘密招募人员组织狙击手小队。他向日本士兵出售淫秽图片——此举有损国家声誉。他向日军泄露了中国军队的军事机密。他与一名叫Heshizima的日本人一起前往日本军事总部，担任中文翻译，审讯被日本人逮捕的中国人。他还陪同日本人以打鸟为借口参观金刚、宝兴精、昆山、六合等重要军事战略要点，目的是带日本人去绘制地图。
叛徒王荣钱，三十多岁，宁波人，居住于杨树浦公大棉纱厂第一宿舍1号。他曾任该厂督察。在1932年1月28日期间，他是日军的间谍。之后他乘坐日本飞机引导军队轰炸江湾。他还带领不良分子在战区抢劫钱财和物品。他还代表日军雇佣了三四百名中国工人，平整公大棉纱厂后面的荒地，将其建成机场。
以下三名叛徒担任日本海军陆战队第三大队总部的间谍：
(1) 谢志成，35岁9个月，居住通州路东海里29号。
(2) 应清祥，37岁，安徽人，居住杨树浦路同兴棉纱厂宿舍66号。

page_data.en:
(3) Waung Ts Koo (王志高), age 40, residing at Hwa Shing Fong
alleyway, off Y'Poo Road.

The above statement is concerning with traitors who have
disclosed secrets. This is very important order. Besides issuing
confidential order to the Detective Corps for close attention, all
of Officers i/c of various districts and/or divisions to make
strict and confidential investigations of the above.

This order is issued by the Clerks' Office for reply, 9/2/choppee
This Order is issued to
Chu Ching (朱青),
Inspector i/c of the 4th Station, 5th Division,
Chopped Vung Oong Ung,
Commissioner of Public Safety Bureau.

Officer i/c of 4th Station, 5th Division.

Immediate delivery,
From Public Safety Bureau,
Shanghai Municipality.
4p.m. 9/2/33.

(3) 王志高，40岁，居住杨树浦路华兴坊弄堂。

以上陈述涉及泄露机密的叛徒。这是一项非常重要的命令。除了向侦探队发出秘密命令予以密切关注外，各区及/或各科的主管官员须对上述人员进行严格且秘密的调查。

此命令由文书处发出以待回复，2月9日盖章
此命令发给
朱青，
第五分区第四捕房主管督察，
盖 翁文光 印，
公共安全局局长。

立即送达，
